nodes.label: Divergence Register
nodes.rationale: What makes "dipertanggungjawabkan" enforceable rather than aspirational: if a reviewer asks why the study deviated from its own specification, the answer is a row here, not improvisation. A contradiction discovered later gets the next free ID and a full row; absorbing one silently is the exact failure this file exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Severity and status scheme (F / C / U / I)
nodes.rationale: F fatal to validity if unresolved, C internal contradiction, U underspecified, I improvement. Status "resolved" means encoded in CLAUDE.md; "open" means an external action is still required.

nodes.label: Second-pass audit provenance — two lenses never ran
nodes.rationale: Three of five adversarial lenses completed; consistency and Kaggle died on a session limit, and the verifier stage died too, so every entry was adjudicated by direct re-derivation against the document text or the artifact on disk. The pass is incomplete by construction, and saying otherwise would be the exact failure the register exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Smaller corrections absorbed without a numbered entry
nodes.rationale: Each was verified and each changes one sentence, not a rule: the DM unit of observation, PT alignment with the trading rule, the seed-averaging order, the log-ratio demotion, the H==L measurement, §11 item 13 in window terms, and the hedged priority claim.

nodes.label: Open items requiring external action
nodes.rationale: D16 citation verification blocks submission; D33 and D26 block Stage 2/Stage 4; the two unrun adversarial lenses block Stage 4 sign-off. D10 and D11 are struck through, closed by D33.

nodes.label: D01 — The K ladder does not add up
nodes.rationale: K=8 summed to nine and log_mean_trade_size was double-assigned. Given the family cardinalities the cut is forced, not chosen: only one assignment of the eight remaining variates satisfies both counts and keeps F2 intact as the redundancy control.

nodes.label: D02 — The K_eff gate reads test-period data
nodes.rationale: A design decision informed by data the design is later evaluated on, with a qualitative trigger ("far below ~6.5") that admits any post-hoc reading. Fixed by the pre-first-origin span and a numeric trigger of PR < 5.0.

nodes.label: D03 — The use_norm verification test cannot pass as written
nodes.rationale: The target is a channel of the same scaled array, so multiplying the input by c multiplies the target by c and the loss by c^2. A team running the source test would see it fail and either disable use_norm or chase a non-existent bug.

nodes.label: D04 — Instance normalisation strips volatility level, confounding RQ1
nodes.rationale: The 8→12 rung can flatten because its information was normalised away — a mechanism entirely distinct from the redundancy the rung was designed to demonstrate. Any channel whose information content is its scale is reduced to its pattern.

nodes.label: D05 — D(b) conflates model decay with market difficulty
nodes.rationale: A rising D(b) is consistent with model decay and with the market simply becoming harder, and the two are not separable; the source already defines RelMSE for period difficulty but never applies it to D(b). A(b) needs no correction because both models see the same block.

nodes.label: D06 — The decay regression is underspecified
nodes.rationale: Without origin fixed effects, between-origin baseline difficulty enters the residual and beta1 is identified partly from cross-origin differences rather than purely from time-since-training.

nodes.label: D07 — The origin count is credited to the wrong cause
nodes.rationale: The 2017-08 claim is false against the declared 2018-01-01 window, and a reader following it would fetch five extra months of data for no gain.

nodes.label: D08 — Horizon sweep K count stated two ways
nodes.rationale: 4 × 4 × 4 × 3 = 192 matches the stated total; 4 × 3 × 4 × 3 = 144 does not, so Stage 8 is the typo.

nodes.label: D09 — Reference library says twelve origins
nodes.rationale: Stale text from the superseded futures-based design, superseded twice over.

nodes.label: D10 — The artifact on disk violates the specification (ffill)
nodes.rationale: Alleged fill_policy=ffill with 122 synthetic bars would fabricate zero-return bars, force H=L=O=C and drive all three F2 estimators to zero immediately before whatever event caused the outage. Closed by D33: none of the three quoted keys exists on the artifact.

nodes.label: D11 — The Stage 1 entry point is missing
nodes.rationale: Provenance must cite a tool that exists and a procedure that can be re-run. Closed by D33: the script exists at the repository root as spot_klines_btc.py.

nodes.label: D12 — signed_flow is a deterministic product of two other K=8 members
nodes.rationale: The product is nonlinear so it is not perfectly redundant, but the "maximum effective rank" claim is weaker than stated; kept because the interaction is the standard order-flow-imbalance construction, with the measured PR left to settle how much rank it contributes.

nodes.label: D13 — F2 estimators: per-bar or trailing-averaged
nodes.rationale: Per-bar with no trailing average: feeding a pre-smoothed estimator is strictly less informative, since the model can compute the average itself but cannot recover what smoothing destroyed. Consequence: no variate uses a rolling window at all, which licenses the no-embargo argument.

nodes.label: D14 — Undefined denominators and a division by zero
nodes.rationale: A bar in which nothing traded carries no trade information, the same condition as downtime, so it takes the same policy — substituting any value would be imputation under another name. Side effect: log(volume), VWAP and the F2 logarithms become total functions.

nodes.label: D15 — Embargo declared justified with no justification
nodes.rationale: Silence on a López de Prado protocol element is exactly what a reviewer familiar with that literature will flag. The two-path argument is only airtight while every variate is a per-bar function.

nodes.label: D16 — Unverified and mis-dated citations
nodes.rationale: The reference library states of itself that volumes, page ranges and DOIs were assembled from search results rather than published versions. Standing rule: no citation enters the manuscript without a verified DOI and the source read.

nodes.label: D17 — No control for "is a transformer needed at all?"
nodes.rationale: Ridge gives a clean two-way decomposition: ridge vs Naive-RW answers does the information help, iTransformer vs ridge answers does the architecture help, K=8 vs K=1 answers does cross-variate attention help. Without ridge the first two are entangled.

nodes.label: D18 — Three seeds is too few for the headline claim
nodes.rationale: A standard deviation estimated from n=3 is itself extremely noisy, and reacting to seed noise after seeing results would be a design change made in response to the outcome.

nodes.label: D19 — "Hours, not days" holds only in one implementation regime
nodes.rationale: The claim is not wrong, it is unconditioned, and the unstated condition is the difference between fitting the weekly quota and blowing through it.

nodes.label: D20 — RelMSE near 1.00 is hard to read
nodes.rationale: R2_oos = 0.004 reads immediately; RelMSE = 0.996 does not. Anything above roughly 0.05 at this horizon should raise a leakage suspicion until re-verified.

nodes.label: D21 — Trading rule and directional accuracy undefined at H=24
nodes.rationale: The choice changes turnover by more than an order of magnitude and dominates every cost-adjusted number in Table 8. The cumulative forecast is what the position actually earns over the holding period; non-overlapping execution prevents the same forecast being traded 24 times.

nodes.label: D22 — No rung tests genuinely nonlinear features
nodes.rationale: An optional K=16 rung supplies a second high-nominal-K / low-K_eff control. It must be an explicit fifth rung; folded into the existing four it destroys the instrument.

nodes.label: D23 — The pre-registered tau is arithmetically unreachable
nodes.rationale: Pure arithmetic on D20's own magnitudes: 1/0.996 − 1 = 0.402%, so all three thresholds demand the model become 2-10% worse than forecasting zero. RQ3 would return a null fixed before a single epoch runs, by a units mismatch rather than by the market.

nodes.label: D24 — No purge at the train/validation boundary
nodes.rationale: The contamination is small (~24 windows) but it lands on the split that decides early stopping and ridge alpha — the split that governs model selection. Validation-window inputs reaching back into training remain legitimate, so the input/target asymmetry is deliberate.

nodes.label: D25 — 17,400 is the 24-month count; training is 21 months
nodes.rationale: The coincidence with the tensor size (80.18 MB) and steps/epoch (545) is decisive: the numbers were derived from 24 months, not from the split. Either every downstream figure inherits a 14% error, or the implementation trains on all 24 months and validates in-sample, which is D24's leak.

nodes.label: D26 — Block index b is collinear with calendar month
nodes.rationale: Settled by one expression: months visited for fixed b form a coset of <s> in Z12 of size 12/gcd(s,12). s=6 gives 2 months, s=3 gives 4, s=5 gives full decoupling. The entry first prescribed 3-month spacing and was corrected in place rather than silently rewritten — the register's own rule applies to the register.

nodes.label: D27 — The Stage 5 gate opens test blocks
nodes.rationale: Idempotence plus a deterministic run_id mean the resume logic finds the pilot runs complete and feeds them verbatim into Table 4 and the beta1 regression, so the origin that decided the framing re-enters the evidence for it. It is a selection event over the paper's conclusion, which the DSR does not correct.

nodes.label: D28 — Consecutive origins share most of their training data
nodes.rationale: Effective independence is bounded by total span / training window ≈ 4 regardless of spacing, so packing origins closer raises nominal G without adding information. At G=3 the disjoint-triple re-estimate will very likely be inconclusive, and that is itself the finding — it bounds what the full-panel p-value can honestly claim.

nodes.label: D29 — Every headline DM comparison is nested
nodes.rationale: Under nested models with estimated parameters the loss differential has a mean shifted away from zero and the statistic is not asymptotically N(0,1), so DM is undersized against exactly the alternative the paper wants to establish — and a viable paper can be killed by the wrong critical value at the Stage 5 gate.

nodes.label: D30 — Seed std is the wrong error bar for origin-aggregated results
nodes.rationale: The two rules in §9.2 contradict each other: seeds are declared non-inferential for the regression and then made the sole uncertainty display for the results table, reintroducing exactly the overstated precision the wild cluster bootstrap was added to prevent.

nodes.label: D31 — y_z = 0 in scaler space is a drift forecast
nodes.rationale: mu_g varies by origin with the bull/bear cycle — the same cycle H2 invokes as its mechanism — so the nuisance is confounded with the effect of interest and does not wash out across origins.

nodes.label: D32 — RQ1's K vs K_eff regression is not identified at three rung deltas
nodes.rationale: Adjacent deltas share an MSE with opposite sign (mechanical correlation ≈ −0.5) and three points plus an intercept leave 1 residual df, so the two specifications cannot be distinguished. The paper is titled after this comparison.

nodes.label: D33 — Empty data/raw and an out-of-window boundary bar
nodes.rationale: The audit's proposed fix — re-derive §4.1 from the report — is rejected because it would bake the out-of-window bar into the measured facts. The defect is in the artifact, not the table. Closes D10 and D11.

nodes.label: D34 — Newey–West Bartlett contradicts the dm.test validation target
nodes.rationale: Under the DM null h-step errors are MA(h−1), so all autocovariances to lag 23 are genuinely nonzero; Bartlett weights shrink gamma-hat_22 by ~92%, understating the long-run variance and producing the over-rejection the paragraph opens by warning against.

nodes.label: D35 — SPA and Reality Check cannot correct a pairwise matrix
nodes.rationale: The diagnosis is right and the remedy is the wrong tool: SPA's null is max_k E[d_k] <= 0 against one benchmark, not a family of pairwise nulls. With 8+ models the matrix holds 28+ tests, expecting ~1.4 spurious rejections under a complete null.

nodes.label: D36 — Figure 3 plots A(b) for four K; A is one series
nodes.rationale: Left unfixed, whoever generates the figure invents a definition, and the figure and the regression then report different quantities under the same symbol — in the paper's graphical abstract. The per-origin-lines form also displays the actual identification.

nodes.label: D37 — The linear-span argument is not a theorem under use_norm
nodes.rationale: Instance normalisation is itself a nonlinearity; d_model=128 > L=96 makes the projection generically injective; and the exclusion list is inconsistent with its own justification, since RSI and Bollinger bands are not linear in the lookback. The structural no-rolling-window consequence survives intact and rests on the twelve definitions, not on the span argument.

nodes.label: D38 — Validation-based hyperparameter selection that never occurs
nodes.rationale: Holding capacity fixed is what makes the rungs comparable, so no per-rung tuning is performed — but as written the flat 8→12 rung has an untested alternative explanation, which one robustness run at larger d_ff closes.

nodes.label: D39 — Target-channel vs all-channel loss unspecified
nodes.rationale: Under an all-channel loss the amount of auxiliary supervision varies with the study's own independent variable, and K=1 is not the stated control but a different learning problem. The reference implementation defaults to the option that breaks the design.

nodes.label: D40 — Baselines carry no K assignment
nodes.rationale: The comparison an LTSF-literate reviewer cares about is iTransformer at K=8 versus PatchTST at K=8 on identical information. If PatchTST silently ran at K=1, the paper's central architectural comparison collapses into univariate-versus-multivariate.

nodes.label: D41 — b* has no estimator, origin index, or censoring method
nodes.rationale: min{.} does not commute with averaging, so pooled and per-origin b* are different estimands. The per-origin values are interval-censored survival data; a bare integer in the abstract violates the manuscript's own "never a bare number" rule.

nodes.label: D42 — The wild cluster bootstrap recipe is incomplete
nodes.rationale: As written, two implementers get different p-values from identical prediction files — the exact failure §12's traceability contract exists to prevent. Every omitted choice (restricted vs unrestricted, studentized, B, alpha, sidedness, t(G−1)) moves the number.

nodes.label: D43 — The leakage surface is declared closed on an incomplete enumeration
nodes.rationale: The no-rolling-window claim checks out; the closure claim built on it does not, because it is scoped to feature construction at the train-test boundary and fails at the first boundary that is not train-test. A closed-surface claim is also what stops the hunt §2 mandates.

nodes.label: D44 — K_eff's span is undeclared and the statistic is blind to cross-lag structure
nodes.rationale: §11 item 5 audits only the gate, so a full-sample RQ1 regressor survives every existing checklist item by construction. And two variates can be near-uncorrelated contemporaneously yet near-redundant to a model with a 96-hour lookback — a measurement-validity failure rather than a finding if unaddressed.

nodes.label: D45 — Window loss is reported globally; per-block it reaches 50%
nodes.rationale: An assertion against a 4.9% global estimate fires spuriously at most origins and would predictably be loosened until it passes — disarming the single defence against the pipeline's most likely silent failure. §4.3 names the bug the assertion exists to catch; specified at the wrong granularity it cannot catch it.

nodes.label: D46 — Unfixed trade phase, gap-spanning returns, unimplementable DSR
nodes.rationale: With N=621 and T=180 the DSR threshold is essentially unmeetable — a second guaranteed null alongside D23, reading to a referee as either a failed strategy or a misapplied statistic with no way to tell which. §13.5 is also the one place returns are computed outside the segment-aware feature code.

nodes.label: D47 — The LR schedule makes the epoch budget decorative
nodes.rationale: Training adequacy is otherwise an alternative explanation for every K contrast: a K=12 model has 12 tokens of attention structure to fit in the same ~7 effective epochs as a K=1 model with none.

nodes.label: D48 — Four outcome-determining choices left open after results
nodes.rationale: A document otherwise scrupulous about pre-registration leaves four levers unfixed — and the pre-registered thresholds are precisely the ones that cost nothing, while slippage, which decides whether the strategy makes money, is blank.

nodes.label: D49 — The flat 8→12 rung has the fewest seeds and no equivalence test
nodes.rationale: "Flat 8→12" is an assertion of no effect, and a non-significant delta is a failure to reject rather than evidence of equivalence — at n=3 a near-guaranteed failure to reject regardless of the truth. The paper would assert the designed contrast without being able to show it.

nodes.label: D50 — The uniform-attention control is never used as an arm
nodes.rationale: K=1 versus K=8 varies information and architecture simultaneously, so a decaying A(b) is equally consistent with a capacity story as with the information story RQ2 claims. Ridge separates them only under a linear model; uniform attention is the only control that does it within the architecture under study.

nodes.label: D54 — The launcher cannot run without a second Dataset
nodes.rationale: Three defects with one root cause: the launcher assumed the repository would be present on the machine that runs it, so §12's traceability contract lost both its code half (git_sha unknown) and its input half (hard-coded report path) at precisely the place the grid executes. Files rather than in-cell definitions, because the grid runs as subprocesses that inherit none of the kernel's namespace.

nodes.label: D54e — Partial sessions crashed the evaluation cells
nodes.rationale: The estimators are right to refuse an unbalanced panel; where the exception landed was not — the last cells of a twelve-hour session, marking the Kaggle version failed at the moment its output was the only thing worth keeping.

nodes.label: D54f — The budget clock started inside each worker
nodes.rationale: Kaggle's 12 h wall runs from the notebook's first cell, so the ~20-25 min prelude sat outside the budget and the two clocks drifted. Hitting the wall interactively loses /kaggle/working entirely, so the margin is not somewhere to be approximate.
